chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from al-'Is, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who comes upon water while he is junub, after he had already prayed. He said: He performs ghusl and does not repeat the salat (prayer).

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer) that had already been performed
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water, meaning the means for ritual purification here
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state requiring ghusl due to major ritual impurity
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he performs ghusl, the ritual bath required for janabah

ai.seo_question: If a junub person prays and later finds water, must he repeat the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a junub person who had prayed and then later found water. Imam Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام states that he must perform ghusl, but he does not need to repeat the salat (prayer) already performed. The narration relates to rulings of ritual purity and the validity of worship performed before water became available.
